title: What is held
description: The things the dialect names and the house holds.
html:
WATER, FIRE, THE EARTH

The forms

IdeGlossEvidence
Mmiliwaterauthority: 'mmili – water'; lexicon class A
Ọkụfirelexicon has it (the fold also reaches òkù call, shout)
Ana / Anaearthnever a headword; the head or tail of anasom, akpati ana, okpuana, Ezeana, osiana, nwuana
Ikukuairlexicon: 'ìkùkù — breeze; wind; gale (Onicha)'
Ufieredauthority: 'ufie – n. red. Etymology: From Onicha Ufie ufie'; lexicon class A
Okilikilicirclelexicon: 'òkìlìkili — round shape (circular, not spherical)'
Ọjịkola nutthe authority's headword is 'oji — bitter kola'. The document writes ọjị, which is the IGBO form (C30 class)
Ajọ Mmụọnegative forcesauthority: 'ajō – adj. bad'; lexicon: 'ajọ mmụọ' class A
Ndụlife; greenlexicon holds ǹdu leadership and ndụ̀ under one folded key
Nkọlọtrianglelexicon: 'nkọlọ̀ — tortoise (borrowed from Ekoid)'. NEEDS A RULING
Uzuspirallexicon: 'ụzụ — blacksmith; blacksmithing (Onicha)'. NEEDS A RULING

Ọkọchịdry seasonneeded vocabulary
